about: The judges' page, /judges/, as one Task Object of words (the AgoraJudges board and backlog O11, November 1, 2026). Every row of 'What is real' is either filled at build time from a record this site holds (the 'fill' names which one: the replayed run, the 1,000 test scenarios, the partner compute record or the feeds index) or says plainly, in present tense, what has not happened. The tour button adds ?tour=judge, which opens the 45-second tour strip. The film is withdrawn until its re-recorded cut lands, so nothing here links it.
title: For judges | Agora
description: Judging ta-amps in five minutes: five steps through Eranos, Agora and the live queue, and a table of what is real and what is an example, each line from a record.
heading: Judging ta-amps in five minutes
lead: Eranos puts spare AI tokens to work for nonprofits. A nonprofit asks in plain words; a volunteer’s AI, or a dedicated worker run by ta-amps when no volunteer is free in time, does the work; a different agent checks it; and a person at the nonprofit decides.

steps.heading: See a real run
steps.text: How it works replays one recorded run step by step: who picked up each part, the model it declared, and its record.

steps.heading: Open the example request
steps.text: REQ-INTAKE-07 on Eranos replays a practice case at reading speed, from the request to the person who decides.

steps.heading: Look underneath
steps.text: The same request in its technical view: the diagram, who held each part, and every step’s record.

steps.heading: Try the queue live
steps.text: In the Studio your browser calls the live Teleion Fabric, its model shim and Eranos, and shows every call and its answer, from claiming a Task to a write that is refused because another came first.

steps.heading: Ask for real
steps.text: Send your own public request on Eranos. We don't accept private information at this stage.

real_heading: What is real, and what is an example
real_lead: Each line comes from a record this site holds, read when the page is built, or says plainly what has not happened.

rows.state: A practice case on Eranos. Nothing in it was sent, built or run; it shows a request’s steps at reading speed.

On {date}, a dedicated worker run by ta-amps built a kit and a second agent with its own key checked it, both running {model}, on a local copy of Teleion Fabric with example data. Every step is recorded.
This site holds no count of volunteers’ work, so this page gives none. Eranos shows its queue as it is now.
They take work that no volunteer picks up in time, and volunteers always get first pick. No run of theirs is on record on this site, and the status check does not cover them.

{total} test scenarios, checked by written rules with no model calls, on one computer, from seed {seed}: {direct} approved as asked, {split} approved after a private and public split, {blocked} blocked.

frontier.heading: Push the Frontier
frontier.lead: The event asks for hard problems where models meet the real world. This is what we can show today, and each line links to the record it comes from.

items.title: A model learned a new skill
items.text: {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}, fine-tuned by ta-amps, filled in tool calls exactly in {after}% of our {n} test cases, up from {before}%.
items.label: Models used

items.title: Work picks its own model
items.text: For each Task, a self-tuning policy picks {{model:muse-spark-1.3}} or {{model:muse-wonder-1.0}}, and a persona, and learns from the recorded results.
items.label: Models used

items.title: Someone else always checks
items.text: In our {date} test run, one agent built a kit in {built}; a second agent with its own key checked it in {checked}. {tests} tests passed and no rule was broken.
items.label: The recorded run

items.title: No work is done twice
items.text: Tasks wait in a durable queue. A worker holds a lease while it works, and a second claim on the same Task gets a conflict instead.
items.label: See it replayed

frontier.footnote: We make no claim here about physical systems or results on partner hardware. Every number here comes from our own recorded tests, and the page fills it in from those records.
